name: repo-memory-v1
about: Twenty-seven things an agent working on this repository would have learned, and sixteen questions it would later need them for. Every entry is a real fact about darkcode as of 2026-08; every gold label is justified in its query's note. Two properties are deliberate. Distractors: several entries share vocabulary with a query they do not answer, because a corpus where the right answer is the only one containing the query's words measures nothing. Two question shapes: some queries are natural language ('why did the knowledge graph get so large') and some name a file or symbol ('what does spill do with a big tool result'). The knowledge-graph signal only fires when a query token matches a node label, so the split is what makes its contribution visible instead of averaged away.

entries.text: replaced the summed retrieval score with reciprocal rank fusion over three signals
entries.content: Vector cosine, keyword overlap and knowledge-graph boost were being added together despite living on different scales, so one signal silently dominated. Rewrote as RRF with k=60 over three separately ranked lists.

entries.text: fixed cosineSimilarity returning NaN on large vectors
entries.content: float64(a[i]*b[i]) does the multiply in float32, which overflows to +Inf near 1e19 and makes the whole score NaN. A NaN does not rank low, it sorts unpredictably. Widened before multiplying.

entries.text: the knowledge graph reached 160MB because nested agent worktrees were indexed
entries.content: 76.7 percent of edges came from .claude/worktrees checkouts of other branches, indexed once per worktree with N-squared cross-worktree symbol references. Filtering the data took it to 15MB.

entries.text: make ci went red with no code change because two scanners counted nested worktrees
entries.content: scripts/arch-check.sh and safeurl/no_bypass_test.go both hand-walk the tree and were counting .claude/worktrees as this branch's violations. llm-calls read 129 against a baseline of 20.

entries.text: the GUI dropped every file_change event because it never subscribed to that type
entries.content: EventSource only delivers a named event to a listener registered for that name. The subscription list in 10-sse.js had 19 of 20 types.

entries.text: the browser read evt.task for a field the wire calls task_id
entries.content: core.UIEvent marshals TaskID as task_id. Four reads used the bare name, so the event-feed type mapping was dead and the live plan board never matched its project.

entries.text: built the data source manager and took orchestrator implementation imports to zero
entries.content: The orchestrator reached into memory directly in ten places. A read gateway composes the existing retriever and graph rather than reimplementing them.

entries.text: extracted adjudication into its own component out of the orchestrator
entries.content: 375 lines deciding between candidate answers. Evidence first, debate only when the graph cannot check the claims, capped at one round.

entries.text: built the vendor-name leak guard as a hook and a CI job
entries.content: One rule set, two layers. Refuses a branch name, commit message or staged filename carrying a vendor name, with an exception for genuine model identifiers in the provider catalogue.

entries.text: deleted the loop's duplicate context-overflow ladder
entries.content: The ReAct loop carried its own refit-and-retry path that modelport already owned. Routing the loop through the model manager made it dead code.

entries.text: the permission judge was running with no token ceiling
entries.content: A model call deciding whether a dangerous tool runs, with its limit left to whatever the provider defaults to. Invisible to every test; only showed up when driven live.

entries.text: stopped embedding the same string three times per request
entries.content: Every episodic and semantic write plus every recall embedded the query independently. Memoised, with embedCacheMax at 512.

entries.text: reciprocal rank fusion constant
entries.content: RRF uses k=60 in memory/retrieval.go. The constant is the published default and damps the difference between adjacent ranks so no single stream can dominate.

entries.text: session epoch and fresh-chat isolation
entries.content: StartNewSession clears short-term memory and advances the session epoch. Episodic recall filters entries older than the epoch so a prior conversation stops resurfacing; durable semantic and graph memory is kept deliberately.

entries.text: the single static binary constraint
entries.content: DarkCode builds with CGO_ENABLED=0 into one static binary with four dependencies. Any storage change must keep that, which is why a pure-Go SQLite driver is the only one considered.

entries.text: architectural boundary baselines are ceilings
entries.content: scripts/arch-check.sh holds a count per boundary in .arch-baseline. A count may fall and never rise. A boundary at zero is enforced.

entries.text: imported skills are authored guidance, not measured experience
entries.content: A skill read from a file has never been tried on this machine, so it starts at a success rate of 0.5 and is marked imported. A learned skill of the same name outranks it and is never overwritten.

entries.text: the cognition cascade rungs
entries.content: A question descends smalltalk, deterministic, cache, graph, recall, then llm. Each rung that answers saves the model call the next one would have made.

entries.text: the free-tier model budget is measured per day
entries.content: A free-tier key with a small daily allowance returns 429 for everything at once when exhausted, which looks exactly like a code bug. Check the log before debugging behaviour that broke all at once.

entries.text: debate is a fallback, not the mechanism
entries.content: Checking claims against the knowledge graph settles a disagreement for zero extra model calls. Debate runs only when the graph cannot check them, and is capped at one round because accuracy plateaus and drift compounds.

entries.text: the GUI runs persistently on port 12345
entries.content: Test against a different port. Web assets are embedded in the binary, so editing JavaScript or HTML does nothing until a rebuild.

entries.text: a typed nil in an interface is not nil
entries.content: Assigning a nil concrete pointer to an interface variable gives a non-nil interface. Guard at the call site rather than comparing the interface to nil.

entries.text: map iteration order must be broken deterministically
entries.content: SemanticAll and the fusion scores range over maps. Any ordering code must break ties on a stable key or retrieval stops being reproducible and the answer cache stops working.

entries.text: the memory write gateway owns placement
entries.content: Every fact the agent learns goes through the recall manager, which decides which of the stores it belongs in. The kernel states what it learned rather than choosing a destination.

entries.text: oversized tool results are offloaded by the spill store instead of truncated
entries.content: A large tool result used to be cut to a fixed budget. spill/spill.go writes it to disk and leaves a preview plus a retrievable handle in the context.

entries.text: confined writes to the working directory in pathguard
entries.content: tools/pathguard.go refuses a write whose resolved path escapes the workspace, symlinks included.

entries.text: modelport purposes select a tier
entries.content: modelport.Ask carries a Purpose - Plan, Execute, Converse, Synthesize, Compress, Classify, Review, Adjudicate - and the manager maps each to an ordered tier preference.

queries.q: why did the knowledge graph get so large
queries.note: One cause, one entry. ep-arch-check-worktrees shares the worktree vocabulary and is a distractor: same root cause, different symptom, and not an answer to a question about size.

queries.q: what constant does reciprocal rank fusion use
queries.note: The semantic fact states the constant; the episodic entry records introducing it. Both are legitimately responsive.

queries.q: how does a fresh chat stop old conversations coming back
queries.note: Only entry describing the epoch filter.

queries.q: a retrieval score came back NaN
queries.note: Direct. sem-rrf-constant and ep-rrf-fusion are scoring distractors.

queries.q: the GUI is not showing something the server emits
queries.note: Two separate defects with the same symptom. A retriever that finds only one has half the answer, which is exactly what R@k should punish.

queries.q: can we switch the graph store to SQLite
queries.note: The constraint that decides it. ep-graph-pollution mentions the graph and its size and is a distractor: it explains why the question came up, not what the answer is.

queries.q: when do two models argue with each other
queries.note: The fact states the gate; the episodic entry records building it.

queries.q: why can a boundary count never go up
queries.note: Single answer. ep-arch-check-worktrees mentions baselines and counts and is a distractor about a failure, not the rule.

queries.q: I edited the JavaScript and nothing changed
queries.note: Embedded assets need a rebuild. ep-sse-file-change and ep-task-id-field are both about GUI JavaScript and are distractors.

queries.q: where should a newly learned fact be written
queries.note: Placement is the gateway's job. sem-imported-skills concerns memory writes too and is a distractor.

queries.q: a nil check passed but the value was nil
queries.note: Single answer, deliberately worded without the words 'typed' or 'interface' so it is not a lexical gimme.

queries.q: what does spill do with a big tool result
queries.note: Names the component. The graph holds file:spill/spill.go, whose label shares the token 'spill' with the query, so this is a query the kg signal is designed to serve.

queries.q: pathguard and writes outside the workspace
queries.note: Same shape: a symbol-named query, which is how a developer actually asks about code.

queries.q: which Purpose does modelport use for planning
queries.note: A symbol name rather than a filename, so the graph is matched on a symbol node.
Two entries changed retrieval ranking. 'retrieval' is a token of the file:memory/retrieval.go label, so the graph should lift both.
